title: Tiered degradation credit syntax and autoscale-trigger policy for Dedicated throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a deterministic, tiered crediting and remediation model for Dedicated capacity throughput SLA degradations, plus the autoscale-trigger policy and contract wording to be used in customer agreements. The goal is to: 1) minimize ambiguous credit calculations, 2) provide automated, observable remediation steps (autoscale/fallback) that customers can rely on, and 3) include clear contract language for credits and notice windows.
acceptance_criteria: A condensed SLA definition describing throughput commitment, measurement window, and success metrics is drafted and approved by legal.
A deterministic error-budget formula and tiered credit table (no free-form manual credits) is published in the contract annex.
Autoscale-trigger policy implemented in the Dedicated control-plane (spec, not full code) with threshold knobs documented.
Monitoring queries/dashboards and alerts for SLA breach and credit burn are defined and linked.
Remediation playbook (automatic + manual escalation) is documented and validated with an internal tabletop run.
Pilot customers (2) have agreed to the pilot credit semantics and opt-in rollout plan.
Legal approves the final contract language and the release notes are prepared for Sales/AM teams.
proposed_contract_language: Throughput Commitment: Redwood will provide a sustained throughput of N RPS per committed GPU (as defined in Schedule A) measured over a rolling 24-hour window with an objective of 99.5% of minutes meeting the target (the 'Throughput SLO').

Error Budget & Credits: If Redwood fails to meet the Throughput SLO for the measurement window, the customer will be eligible for service credits calculated using the Tiered Degradation Table (Section X). Credits are applied monthly and are the sole financial remedy for throughput degradation, except as otherwise provided under applicable law.
Tiered Degradation Table example: Degradation 0.5-2% => 5% of monthly Dedicated fee; 2-10% => 15% credit; >10% => 35% credit, subject to a maximum of 50% of monthly Dedicated fee.

Notice & Timing: Customer must report suspected SLA breach to Redwood within 14 days. Redwood will reconcile metrics and apply credits within the next billing cycle. Disagreements follow dispute resolution in Section Y.

Autoscale Exception: If automatic remediation (autoscale burst or fallback to compatible model variants) is executed by Redwood within the remediation window, credits will be reduced by a fixed offset in the Tiered Table (see Section X.3). This incentivizes rapid automated remediation while providing predictable credit exposure.
measurement_spec: Primary metric: sustained_throughput_ok (boolean per minute) where true = achieved >= committed_RPS and p99_latency <= committed_p99_ms for the minute.
Aggregation: Rolling 24-hour window; SLO evaluated as percentage of minutes where sustained_throughput_ok == true.
Thresholds: SLO target = 99.5% of minutes in window; Breach if metric < 99.5%.
Error budget computation: error_budget_burn = max(0, (SLO_target - observed_percentage) / SLO_target) expressed as percent of monthly budget.
Edge cases: Scheduled maintenance windows (declared 72+ hours in advance) are excluded from measurement. Force majeure events and customer misconfiguration are excluded per Section Z.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: SLA-Breach-Warn when 24h rolling SLO < 99.8% (warning), destinations: #dedicated-slo-alerts, paging for high-tier customers.
Alert: SLA-Breach-Critical when 24h rolling SLO < 99.5%, triggers automated remediation workflow and pages on-call infra.
Dashboard: 'Dedicated - Throughput SLO' with minute-level sustained_throughput_ok, rolling SLO curve, credit liability projection for current month.
Monitoring queries: include attribution tags for customer_id, region, model_variant, and hardware_pool to isolate root cause quickly.
Runbooks: link to the remediation runbook and the billing reconciliation sheet for credits computation.
remediation_playbook: Step 0: Detect - Monitoring generates SLA-Breach-Critical and populates incident with autoscale-run id.
Step 1: Auto-remediate - control-plane attempts one automated action: autoscale burst up to configured cap OR route to backup compatible model variant with pre-approved quality delta.
Step 2: Evaluate - after auto-action, measure sustained_throughput_ok for next 60 minutes; if recovered, mark incident as auto-resolved and record reduced credit per contract offset.
Step 3: Manual follow-up - if auto-action fails, on-call infra executes manual scale and opens RCA ticket. Customer success is notified and a partial credit calculation begins.
Step 4: Finalize credit - finance applies deterministic credit from Tiered Degradation Table and notifies customer with reconciliation report, normally within billing cycle.
Step 5: Postmortem - incident owners publish a short RCA to the customer-facing incident summary within 5 business days and propose mitigations for recurring breaches.
autoscale_trigger_policy: Primary triggers: sustained_throughput_ok == false for 3 consecutive minutes AND observed_queue_length > threshold_for_3min.
Severity scaling: If breach persists for 15 minutes, allow burst up to 2x committed GPUs for customers with burst-enabled entitlements; otherwise, run fallback to quantized model variant.
Knobs exposed to customers: burst_enabled (true/false), burst_cap (1.5x|2x|3x), fallback_policy (none|auto|manual-approve).
Safety constraints: maximum burst duration 30 minutes per incident and global cluster caps to prevent noisy-neighbor cascades.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Documentation and contract draft complete; internal review with Legal, Finance, and Infra owners.
Week 2: Feature flagged autoscale policy deployed to internal test orgs; run two induced SLA breach scenarios and validate credit math end-to-end.
Week 3-4: Pilot with 2 selected Dedicated customers (one with burst_enabled, one without) for 30 days and collect feedback.
Week 5: Address feedback, finalize contract annex, and update sales playbook + TOS addendum.
Week 6: General availability for new Dedicated contracts; existing customers can opt-in via amendment.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-03-01: Use deterministic tiered credits rather than subjective per-incident negotiations to improve predictability for both sides.
Decision 2026-03-03: Apply a credit offset when automatic remediation successfully restores throughput within the remediation window to reward automated action.
Trade-off: Deterministic credits may not fully cover bespoke commercial disputes; sales retains ability to negotiate case-by-case credits as an exception handled by Finance/Legal.
Open question: whether to expose SLO computation to customers via read-only query endpoint. Initial pilot will not expose raw SLO query API, instead provide reconciled monthly reports.
